title: Night sky at Paranal
caption: Star trails, a laser and the Magellanic Clouds over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars leave trails across the night sky over Paranal Observatory, visible on the mountain at right. From one of the telescopes, an orange beam of light reaches up into the darkness, and higher in the sky float two elongated, cloud-like shapes.

The orange beam is a laser, used to measure turbulence in the atmosphere. In a single quick snapshot it would be a thin line. Because the camera collected light for so long, the beam has spread out into a wide fan instead.

The two cloudy shapes are the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds, dwarf galaxies that surround our own Milky Way. Because of the long exposure, the whole picture records a stretch of time rather than a single instant: the stars became trails and the laser became a fan.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye would see the laser as a thin line and the stars as points; the long exposure turns them into a fan and trails.

explore: The star trails themselves come from Earth's rotation: as the planet turns, the camera turns with it, and each star's light is drawn out along the sky. Only the ground stays still.
alt: Star trails over a mountain observatory on the right, with an orange laser fan rising from a telescope and two cloudy galaxies in the sky.
